history.summary: A 2005 99LH 3BR in Hillview (D23) at $1.38M / $1,221 psf, with a robust URA dataset (118 txns, 4.46%/yr resale CAGR) and PSF only ~3% above median. Solid, liquid, fairly-priced mass-market unit but with ~78 years of lease left and no standout catalyst.
history.rating_rationale: 118 URA transactions give high confidence in the 4.46%/yr appreciation — a healthy, reliable OCR rate. PSF $1,221 vs median $1,188 is fair (≈+3%), a generous 1,130 sqft 3BR, and $1.38M is a deeply liquid family ticket. Offsetting: 2005 vintage means ~78yr lease remaining and lease decay starts mattering on a 5-7yr hold-then-resell; Hillview is well-served (Hillview MRT/DTL) but lacks a fresh upside catalyst. Net: a sound, unexciting hold.

MRT distance not specified in listing (Hillview DTL serves the area but walk may be moderate)
catalysts: Reliable 4.46%/yr URA appreciation backed by 118 transactions

history.summary: A 1,152 sqft '3BR' at Hillview Regency (26 Bukit Batok East Ave 2, 99LH from 2000) asking $1.28M / $1,111 psf — the cheapest of 12 live asks in the project and the top 2% of the scored book (score_1000 769). The discount does not survive inspection: 1,152 sqft is a low-floor format at this project (both URA prints ever recorded at that exact size are floor 01-05), and low-floor 1,071-1,233 sqft units clear at a $1,056 psf median vs $1,194 for floors 6+. Against its true cohort the ask is +5.2% ABOVE market, not -7% below it.
history.rating_rationale: The one robust forward signal in this model is cheap-vs-peers, and this unit does not have it once the comp set is drawn correctly. Benchmarked against the whole 1,071-1,233 sqft band (n=29, 24mo) the $1,111 psf ask looks -7.0% cheap, which is what drove score_1000 to 769 (psf_value +5.36, age_value +11.78, rank_norm 0.981). But URA's Floor Level column splits that band cleanly in two: the four sub-$1,100 psf prints in 24 months are ALL floor 01-05, and the tiers are $1,056 psf median (01-05, n=4) vs $1,194 psf (floors 6+, n=25) — an ~11.6% structural floor gap. Both prints ever recorded at exactly 1,152 sqft are floor 01-05 (Oct-2021 $925k/$803psf; Dec-2024 $1,220,000/$1,059psf), i.e. a 100% low-floor share. Priced against that cohort the ask is +5.2% above median, and +4.9% above the Dec-2024 same-size print in ~20 months while the project's own band median went sideways ($1,194 24mo vs $1,191 12mo). So there is no value edge — the apparent one is the floor. The v3.8 print-contradiction rule missed it because the +/-7% size tolerance (1,071-1,233 sqft) is wider than this project's separation between its ground format (1,152) and its tower stacks (1,109/1,119/1,130): the low-floor share dilutes from 100% at the exact size to 14% across the band, under the 0.7 trigger, and no stack keys reached factual_data at all. Second, unresolved question: the condo directories put 1,152 sqft at the TOP of the 2-bedroom / 2+study+balcony line (904-1,152), with true 3BRs at 1,109-1,195 — and the subject is the only 1,152 in a 12-listing live book otherwise made of 1,109/1,119/1,130/1,195. bed_bands returns 'ok' but only at 100-sqft bucket resolution (band 1150, 174 contracts), which cannot separate 1,119/1,130/1,152 — the documented overlap blindspot. A ground unit whose strata area is padded by PES would explain both the size and the PSF. Unverified, but it is the buyer's risk, not the seller's. Third, the -15.7% vs the age-adjusted D23 median is a sub-market level, not a dislocation: despite the name this is Bukit Batok East on the NSL (Bukit Batok 867m, Bukit Gombak 946m), not the Hillview/Dairy Farm DTL enclave, and the project has always traded ~20% under the blended D23 median. Do not double-count it as value. What is genuinely good is the exit record, not this entry: REALSCORE 3.6, 92.5% of 626 resales profitable (576 vs 50), avg holding 7.2yr, 4.3% avg annualized profit over the past year, 572 units and 1,177 lifetime transactions. That is real downside evidence — but it is backward-looking and era-driven (owners entered at 2000s prices; the project is already +38% since 2019), and it argues the development is safe, not that this ask is cheap. Net: a fairly-to-fully-priced low-floor unit in a liquid but unremarkable OCR leasehold, on 73 years of lease, at 3.75% gross / ~2.2% net carry, with no cheapness edge and an open format question. Avoid at $1.28M. The call is explicitly conditional: if viewing establishes this is a genuine mid/high-floor 3BR, the $1,111 psf becomes a real ~7% discount to the $1,194 cohort and this flips to a Buy — confirm the floor and the bedroom count before anything else.
red_flags: Apparent -7% discount is a floor artifact: both URA prints ever at 1,152 sqft are floor 01-05; low-floor cohort median is $1,056 psf, so the ask is +5.2% ABOVE its true comp set

Possible bedroom relabel: condo directories place 1,152 sqft at the top of the 2BR / 2+study+balcony range (904-1,152); true 3BRs are 1,109-1,195. bed_bands 'ok' is only 100-sqft-bucket resolution and cannot discriminate
Only 1,152 sqft unit in a 12-listing live book (others 1,109/1,119/1,130/1,195) — a rare format, likely ground/PES, which is the slowest-exiting slice

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: realsmart: median rent $4,000/mo across the 12 latest contracts (range $3,400-$4,550), avg $3.63 psf, 38 contracts in the past month, est. project yield 3.6%. The scorer used $4,200 (URA project-bed average, 49 contracts, conf 0.95) for a 3.94% gross / 2.37% net. Both are defensible at project level, but a low-floor unit lets at the bottom of the range, so ~$3,800-4,000 is the realistic figure here: ~3.6% gross, ~2.1-2.2% net. Rental demand itself is deep and not the problem — 38 contracts a month on 572 units is a well-let project. Treat this as carry only; per the backtest, high gross yield predicts LOWER forward price growth (std_beta -0.16).
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: URA cache: 4.46%/yr 5yr CAGR on 118 transactions, momentum -0.757 (decelerating). realsmart's annual medians run $874 (2019) -> $1,210 psf (2026), +38.4% / ~4.75%/yr, and 4.3% avg annualized profit for sellers over the past year. All of it is trailing, and the current priors put trailing CAGR/momentum at ~0 forward power once clustered (univariate +0.13) — story, not signal. I am NOT overriding the rate. The forward case rests on the OCR region prior (+3.7%/yr) minus the absence of any value edge, and the project's own 3BR band has gone sideways over the last 12 months ($1,194 psf 24mo median vs $1,191 12mo) after the 2021-2024 run. Note the 2019->2026 pooled figure carries the usual size-mix caveat (realsmart flags it explicitly on the page).
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No researched profile exists for Hillview Regency (stack_profile: not_researched), so this is reconstructed from URA's Floor Level column across all 118 prints. The project's formats separate cleanly by size AND floor: 1,109 sqft (n=21) is 0% low-floor, 1,130 (n=22) 0%, 1,195 (n=13) 0%, 1,173 (n=3) 0%; 1,119 (n=20) is 30% low-floor; and 904 (42%) / 969 (62%) / 1,152 (100%, n=2) carry the ground stock. 24mo tier medians in the 1,071-1,233 band: fl 01-05 $1,056 (n=4), fl 06-10 $1,196 (n=2), fl 11-15 $1,194 (n=7), fl 16-20 $1,197 (n=9), fl 21-25 $1,194 (n=7) — the market prices ONE break, ground vs everything above, worth ~11.6%. The subject's 1,152 sqft sits entirely on the wrong side of it on the evidence available. Caveat honestly: n=2 at exactly 1,152 sqft is thin, PropertyGuru served no floor_level for this listing, and facing is never available from the feed. Worth running /research-development on Hillview Regency — 572 units and 12 live asks justify a real stack profile, and the ground-vs-tower break is the single fact that decides every listing here.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: No override — URA 4.46%/yr on 118 txns retained; trailing CAGR has ~0 forward power under current priors and realsmart's 4.75%/yr agrees closely.
